anomalies.observed: In the WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES block, the populated LiDAR PR7 is wired straight onto the main I2C bus through header H7/P2: PR7.SCL lands on NET0036 (the I2C_SDA net) and PR7.GND lands on NET0007 (the I2C_SCL net). NET0007 is the same net used as I2C_SCL everywhere else (M4A pin 105/I2C_SCL, M3 ATLAS_EZO_RTD TX/SCL, and the SCL2 pins of both ADM3260 isolators U5/U6).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the TF-Luna LiDAR is not implemented in this revision: 'its pins are "free" and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from the board; it is not wired into any net.' Even if a LiDAR were to be added, its GND pin must go to ground and SCL to the SCL net — not GND onto the I2C_SCL line. The main I2C SCL (NET0007) must not be tied to ground.

evidence.quote: PR7 LiDAR pins VCC/SCL/GND/TX/RX row-mapped to header H7 pins 1/2/3/4/5; H7 pin2 = NET0036, H7 pin3 = NET0007 (page 1, WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES)
M3 ATLAS_EZO_RTD TX/SCL -> NET0007; M4A pin 105/I2C_SCL -> NET0007; U6/U5 SCL2 -> NET0007 (page 1, I2C SENSORS / SoC)
PR1 ... its pins are "free" and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from the board; it is not wired into any net.

anomalies.impact: With PR7 populated (no DNP mark, unlike PR8/PR2), the LiDAR's GND pin shorts the entire main I2C SCL bus (NET0007) to ground, and the LiDAR SCL pin is cross-tied to SDA. The main I2C bus (RTD, both isolator primaries, H5/H6 env headers) is dead, so the controller cannot read any sensor on that bus.

anomalies.observed: In the POWER TRAIN block a second ESP32-C6-DEVKIT, M4B, is drawn as a '5V-3.3V 0.8A LDO'. Its 5V0 input pin (11.14) carries a no-connect marker, while its 3V3 output pin (11.15) is tied directly to the +3V3 rail that is also driven by U3 (AZ1117-3.3).
anomalies.expected: The specification's power architecture uses a single 5V->3.3V LDO (AZ1117, U2/U3) for +3V3 and lists only one ESP32-C6 DevKit (M1) as the controller; no second DevKit-as-LDO is described. Tying the 3V3 pin of an unpowered (5V0 open) regulator module to the live +3V3 rail back-feeds the dead module's 3V3 rail and parallels two LDO outputs, which is not sound practice.

evidence.quote: M4B ESP32-C6-DEVKIT, '5V-3.3V 0.8A LDO', pin 11.14 (5V0) marked NC, pin 11.15 (3V3) -> +3V3 (page 1, POWER TRAIN top-right)
U2 — AZ1117-3.3 ... 5 V -> 3.3 V LDO ... VO feeds +3V3, which powers the I2C pull-ups, isolator primary sides, and TMC2209 logic.

anomalies.impact: Back-powering the 3V3 pin of an unpowered DevKit module can partially energise its onboard ESP32-C6 (undefined current draw / possible latch-up) and loads the +3V3 rail; the second LDO serves no designed purpose.
